title: The Iron That Floated Up
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Beside the river, chopping wood,
a man swung hard, then, splash!
The borrowed axe head flew right off
and sank down in a flash.

[Chorus]
Nothing’s too small to tell the Lord,
a toy, a tear, a fear.
He helped with just one lost axe head;
He cares for you, my dear.

[Verse 2]
“Oh no! It wasn’t even mine!”
he said. “What will I do?”
Elisha tossed a stick, and up
the axe head floated too!

[Chorus]

[Verse 3]
Now close your eyes and tell Him all
the little things you keep.
Heavenly Father listens close
and holds you as you sleep.

[Chorus]
mood: Floating music. A light, drifting sway under the voice, the way something rises slowly through water, buoyant and unhurried. The verses keep a small ripple going and the chorus lifts, soft and reassuring, like a hand reaching to catch something small. By the last verse the drift slows and drops low, until the river is still and the child is held.
